Axiom: - Business logic depends on Ports, not Adapters, when a Port exists. Port is preferred: preconditions / postconditions / invariants live on the Port, and the Adapter references it and describes side effects + runtime backing + verification levels. When the module consciously forgoes a Port (single implementation, no confirmed variability or test seam), the same DbC contract lives directly on the Service / Adapter instead — the absence of a Port is not the absence of a contract; that choice is recorded in the Decision Log (`AX_DECISION_LOG_REQUIRED`). - Port introduced only with confirmed v1 variability (≥2 implementations) or explicit test seam. Single implementation without confirmed split → Service or Entity, not Port. - Every proposed abstraction requires justification: which current risk / constraint / consumer it closes. - **Contract obligation follows BEHAVIOR, not entity type.** Any entity that owns behavior — its own state, a lifecycle, error handling, or direct user interaction — carries a DbC contract (Pre / Post / On-violation per operation, plus loading/empty/error states where they apply), a UI component included; "component" is not a free pass. Only a purely-rendering entity (props in, markup out, zero decisions) is exempt, and the exemption must be an explicit `Presentation-Only` marker on that entity's Entity Surface (`ENTITY_SURFACE_FORMAT`) — an entity with neither a contract nor that marker is a spec omission, not a legitimate style choice. - **DbC section shape is flexible.** `Module Contracts (DbC)` carries any subset of subsections drawn from the entity Type vocabulary (Port, Adapter, Service, Component, Pattern, Utility, Module-level invariants, …). Ports/Adapters are AVAILABLE, not mandatory: single-implementation modules legitimately use Service-only, Component-only, or Pattern-only DbC. Subsections are unnumbered `###` headers (e.g. `### Ports`, `### Components`, `### OperationDef Pattern`).
